blocks.text: Preface to the Sutra of the Precious Lankavatara

inline.s: Composed by Jiang Zhiqi, Court Counsellor, Auxiliary Director of Transport with concurrent charge over salt and alum for the Jianghuai, Jing, and Zhe circuits, Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, Bearer of the Purple Gold Fish-Bag, and Lord of the Upper Guards.

Zhiqi once suffered from the Lankavatara Sutra being hard to read and a good edition being hard to find, when it happened that Lord Zhang, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and retired Councillor, gave this sutra at the Southern Capital, and Su Zizhan of Meishan wrote it out and had it cut on woodblocks to become an endowment of Jinshan Monastery. The Elder of Jinshan, Master Foyin Liaoyuan, sent it to me, and Zhiqi spoke of it thus: the sutras spoken by the Buddha comprise twelve divisions in all, and their number reaches five thousand scrolls. In the age when the true Dharma prevailed, there were people who, hearing half a verse or gaining a single phrase, awakened and entered; these cannot be counted. But after the age of the semblance Dharma and the age of the final Dharma, when men had gone far from the Sage, they began to drown in words, suffering the hardship of entering the sea to count the sands, while of the one true substance they remained wholly unaware. Then the patriarchs appeared, pointing directly at the human mind so that one sees the nature and becomes a Buddha, holding this to be a transmission outside the teachings; and in the space of a gesture or a word, those of sharp faculties and keen capacity had already caught it with a glance. Thus Yunmen went so far as to curse the Buddha, and Yaoshan went so far as to forbid men to read the sutras: both meant this. From this, departing from the Buddha, it was called Chan, and leaving doctrine behind, it was called the profound; and so students of the Buddha invariably denounced Chan, and those who shunned doctrine invariably honored the profound. The followers of these two houses attacked one another without knowing that they serve each other's use. And Chan is one of the six perfections; how could it be different from the Buddha?

Zhiqi holds that Chan issues from the Buddha and the profound issues from doctrine; if one does not discard Chan for the Buddha's sake, nor discard doctrine for the profound's sake, then one comes near to it. Ran Qiu asked: "Shall I put it into practice as soon as I hear it?" Confucius said: "Put it into practice as soon as you hear it." Zilu asked: "Shall I put it into practice as soon as I hear it?" and he said: "Your father and elder brother are still alive; how could you do so at once?" That Qiu was told to act at once was because Qiu held back, and so he was urged forward; that You was held back was because You was a match for two men, and so he was restrained. Do teachings then have any fixed rule? They only rescue what is one-sided. When the corruption of Buddha-study reaches the point that men drown in texts and are deluded by the meaning of phrases, so that they do not embody the profound, then one speaks of Chan to rescue them. When the corruption of Chan-study reaches the point that men gallop after empty words and dally with subtle disputation, so that they do not understand the meaning, then one speaks of the Buddha to rescue them. The two rescue each other, and the Buddha-Dharma is complete.

Long ago, when Bodhidharma came from the West, having already transmitted the mind-seal to the Second Patriarch, he said besides: "I have the Lankavatara Sutra in four fascicles; with it I also entrust you. This is the essential gateway of the Tathagata's mind-ground, whereby all beings are opened, shown, awakened, and entered." This too is the Buddha and Chan transmitted together, the profound and doctrine both entrusted. But by the Fifth Patriarch it was changed at last to the Diamond Sutra for transmission, and so the Sixth Patriarch, hearing a guest recite the Diamond Sutra, asked him where it came from. The guest said: "I come from the Fifth Patriarch's mountain east of Huangmei County in Qizhou. The Great Master of the Fifth Patriarch constantly urges monks and laity: simply uphold the Diamond Sutra, and you will of yourself see the nature and become a Buddha." Thus it was with the Fifth Patriarch that the upholding of the Diamond Sutra began. Therefore the Diamond Sutra has flourished greatly in the world, while the Lankavatara has had no transmission at all.

That it is transmitted today is truly due to Lord Zhang's initiative. Zhiqi passed through the Southern Capital and paid his respects to Lord Zhang, hearing from his own mouth the karmic story of the Lankavatara. To begin with, when Lord Zhang went out from the Three Fiscal Commissions and the Hanlin Academy to serve as prefect of Chu, one day he entered the quarters of the monks of Langya and, seeing a sutra-box, opened and looked into it: it was the Lankavatara Sutra. He was suddenly struck with the sense that this was what he himself had written in a former life, and the strokes of the brush were exactly as they were; surely the spirits had received it beforehand, and this is very clear. Zhiqi has heard that when Yang Hu was five years old, he told his wet-nurse to fetch the gold ring he used to play with. The nurse said to him: "You never had such a thing." Hu then went himself to the neighbor Li family's eastern wall and brought it out from among the mulberry trees. The master of the house cried out in astonishment: "This is what my dead son lost! How are you taking it away?" The nurse told the whole story, and so it was known that Hu's former body had been a son of the Li family. Bai Letian was seven months old when his nurse pointed to the two characters "no" and "none," and though he was tested a hundred times over, he never missed; by nine he knew the tones and rules of verse. The historians took him for one deeply endowed in talent and literary grace, but Letian himself firmly held it to be the working of habits from a former life.

By this one true and undying nature, man dies and is born, comes and goes, within heaven and earth. The number of his lives in the world could not be reckoned though all the plants and trees of the world were broken into tally-sticks and counters. Yet because he is sunk in birth and death, his spirit-consciousness grows weary and spent and can no longer remember; only one whose perfect brightness is undimmed knows it. Thus Lord Zhang, by whose lofty writings and great scrolls he again passed the imperial examination and entered the imperial retinue, who held the balance of government and came and went in the court for more than forty years, whose excellence and achievements are spread through men's ears and eyes: that in a former body he was once a great good friend of the Way admits of no doubt. That he could remember the affairs of a former life — is it not truly so? Therefore, having read the new Lankavatara text, I record its karmic story at the head of the sutra.

inline.s: Written out by Su Shi, Court Counsellor and newly appointed Prefect of Dengzhou, with concurrent charge of encouraging agriculture within the jurisdiction, Commandant of Light Cavalry, and Bearer of the Crimson Robe.

The Sutra of the Precious Lankavatara is the subtle, foremost, true and definitive teaching spoken by former Buddhas, and so it is called the All Buddha-Words Mind Chapter. The Patriarch Bodhidharma entrusted it to the Second Patriarch, saying: "I observe that of all the teachings of the scriptures in China, only the Lankavatara in four fascicles can seal the mind." Patriarch transmitted it to patriarch and took it as the mind-dharma. It is like the Classic of Difficulties among physicians: every sentence is principle, every character is a rule. Those who later attain it illuminate it with spirit, like a pearl rolling on a dish, like a dish rolling on a pearl, and nothing is impossible. But to bring forth new ideas and cast aside the old learning as useless — that is either folly without knowledge or madness. In recent years students have each taken their own master as their school, striving after the easy and the brief, and having gained a phrase or a verse, they claim to have realized it themselves, until even women and children clap their hands and laugh, vying to talk of the joy of Chan. The lofty do it for fame, the lowly for profit, and its waves and eddies reach everywhere, so that the Buddha-Dharma has dwindled. It is like a village physician who, without using the treatises, directly hands out prescriptions and medicines to cure illness: it is not that he never hits the mark; but when it comes to meeting an illness and at once judging life and death by conjecture, he cannot be spoken of in the same day as one who knows the classics and studies the ancients. The world sees only that he has a single lucky success, or is quicker than the ancients, and therefore says the Classic of Difficulties may be left unstudied — is this not a mistake!
The meaning of the Lankavatara trends toward the deep and
the boundless

, and its words are terse and ancient. Readers may fail even to punctuate it, let alone set aside the text to gain the meaning, or forget the meaning to understand the mind. This is why it has been so still and desolate in the world, all but lost and barely preserved. Lord Zhang Andao, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Master of Complete Joy, by his vast and great mind attained the pure enlightenment. In the Qingli era he once governed Chu, and coming to a monk's cell he happened upon this sutra; taking it in hand he was dazed, as though he had recovered an old possession. Before the scroll was finished, the barriers of former lives melted like ice, and closely examining the strokes, the handwriting was exactly his own. He sighed in sorrow and joy, and from this awakened and entered; he constantly used the first four verses of the sutra to bring forth the essentials of the mind. Shi has wandered at your gate, my Lord, for thirty years; this year in the second month he passed through the Southern Capital and saw you in your private residence. You were then seventy-nine years of age, illusion extinguished and utterly spent, your light of grace whole and round; and Shi too had grown old in sorrow and trouble, with a hundred thoughts burned cold. You judged me fit to be taught, and so gave me this sutra, and further gave three hundred thousand cash to have it printed and distributed through the Jianghuai region. But the Elder of Jinshan, Master Foyin Liaoyuan, said: "Printing and distributing have an end; if it is written out and cut on blocks, it will have no end." Shi therefore wrote it out, and Yuan sent his attendant Xiaoji to Qiantang to seek a good craftsman to cut the blocks, and so it became an endowment of Jinshan.
The ninth day of the ninth month of the eighth year of the Yuanfeng era (1085).
All Buddha-Words Mind Chapter, Part One of One
Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was dwelling on the peak of Mount Lanka by the shore of the southern sea, adorned with all kinds of precious flowers, together with a great assembly of bhiksus and a great assembly of bodhisattvas who had come from all those manifold Buddha-lands. These bodhisattva-mahasattvas possessed the power of sovereign mastery in measureless samadhi and the play of spiritual powers, and Mahamati Bodhisattva Mahasattva was their chief. All the Buddhas poured the consecration upon their crowns; they understood well the meaning of the realm displayed by their own minds. Toward beings of every kind, with every kind of mind and form, they manifested universally in accord with their classes through measureless gates of deliverance. In the five dharmas, the self-natures, the consciousness, and the two kinds of selflessness, they were thoroughly and completely penetrating.

At that time Mahamati Bodhisattva, together with the Bodhisattva Mati, having journeyed through all the Buddha-lands, by the Buddha's spiritual power rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, placed their right knees on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence praised him in verse:
The world, from birth and death apart, is like a flower in space;
And wisdom, knowing neither yes nor no, brings compassion to the race.
All dharmas are like fantasies, from mind and thought apart,
Beyond both ending and eternity, the world is like a dream.
Who knows both person and dharma are without self; afflictions and the knowable
Are ever pure and without marks, and so he brings forth a mind of compassion.
In all there is no nirvana, nor is there a Buddha in nirvana,
No Buddha who enters nirvana, far beyond the known and the knower.
If there be being and non-being, he leaves the two entirely behind;
The Sage's contemplation of stillness, this it is to be far from birth.
This is what is called non-grasping; this life and the next are pure.”
Then Mahamati Bodhisattva, having praised the Buddha in verse, spoke his own name:
My name is Mahamati, and I fully understand the Great Vehicle.
Now with a hundred and eight meanings I respectfully ask the foremost of the honored.”
The great being who understands the world, hearing the verses he had spoken,
Observed the whole assembly and said to the Buddha's sons:
You sons of the Buddha, ask now freely whatever you wish;
I shall speak for you of the realm of self-realization.”
Then Mahamati Bodhisattva Mahasattva, having received the Buddha's consent, bowed his head at the Buddha's feet, joined his palms in reverence, and asked in verse:
How is one's thought made pure? And how does thought increase?
How is delusion seen? And how does delusion grow?
For what reason are lands transformed, and what are the non-Buddhist paths?
Why is there no receiving of desire? And why is it named no receiving?
Why is one named a Buddha's son? And where does liberation lead?
Who is it that binds, and who is freed? What is the realm of dhyana?
Why are there three vehicles? I pray you, explain it for me.
From what does dependent arising arise? And how is the made made?
How is there both and neither? And what is it that increases?
What is the formless absorption, and what is the trance of cessation?
What is the cessation of perception? From what cause does one wake from absorption?
What is it that is born of action, and how does one come and go and keep the body?
What is manifest discrimination? And how are the stages born?
Who is it that breaks the three existences? Where and how is his body?
Where does the reborn one go? And who is the foremost of sons?
By what cause is spiritual power gained, and sovereign samadhi?
What is the mind of samadhi? Speak it for me, O foremost.
What is it that is named the storehouse? What are mind and consciousness?
How are birth and ceasing? And how does one see and withdraw?
What is the lineage, the non-lineage, and the measure of mind?
How are the established marks set up, and what is the meaning of no-self?
How is there no being? And what is the world's convention?
What is the view of annihilation, and how does the view of eternity not arise?
How is it that the Buddha and the non-Buddhists do not contradict each other in marks?
What are the many different schools of the world to come?
What is emptiness, and from what cause? How does the moment perish?
How is birth from the womb? And how is the world unmoving?
By what cause is it like an illusion, a dream,
A city of the gandharvas, the world's mirage, and the moon in the water?
By what cause are the limbs of awakening taught, and the factors of bodhi?
How is a land in disorder? And how is a view of being made?
How is there no birth and no ceasing, the world like a flower in space?
How is the world awakened to? And how is the letter-free spoken?
Who is it that is far from false imagination? And what is the simile of space?
As what they are, how many kinds are there? How many are minds of the perfections?
By what cause does one pass through the stages? And who reaches the unreceived?
What are the two selflessnesses? And how is the knowable made pure?
How many kinds of wisdom are there? And how many natures of beings by precept?
Who brings forth the natures of jewels, the mani gem and the rest?
Who brings forth the languages, and the many kinds of beings?
The fields of knowledge and the crafts, by whom are they displayed?
How many kinds of gatha are there, long verses and short?
How many kinds of composition are there? And what is it that is named a treatise?
From what are food and drink born, and how are the various desires born?
What is it that is named a king, a wheel-turner or a lesser king?
How is a country guarded? And how many kinds of gods are there?
What is it that is named the earth, the stars, and the sun and moon?
Those who cultivate liberation, how many kinds are there?
How many kinds of disciples are there? And what is an acarya?
How many kinds of Buddha are there, and how many kinds of birth?
The demons and the various non-adepts, how many kinds has each?
The self-nature and the mind, how many kinds has each?
How is the measure established? I pray the foremost, speak.
How are empty wind and cloud? And how is mindfulness clever?
What are the forest trees? And what are the creeping grasses?
What are elephant, horse, and deer? And how are they hunted and caught?
What is lowliness, and by what cause is one lowly?
How are the six teachers gathered in? And what is an icchantika?
Men, women, and the neither-male, how are all these born?
How does cultivation fall back? And how does cultivation go on?
By what dharma does a Chan master establish what manner of men?
Beings are born into the destinies: with what marks, what kinds of form?
What is wealth? And by what cause does wealth come?
What is the Shakya line? And by what cause is there a Shakya line?
What is the sugarcane line? Speak, O Unsurpassed Honored One.
What of the long-suffering sages? How do they teach?
How does the Tathagata appear in every land and every time,
Surrounded by the foremost of sons, in many names and forms?
Why does one not eat meat? And why is the eating of meat forbidden?
The kinds that eat meat, for what cause do they eat meat?
Why are there sun-and-moon-shaped lands, Sumeru, and lotus lands,
Lion-excellent marks of lands, and worlds that stand on edge or overturned,
Like Indra's net, or all of precious jewels,
The harp and the narrow-waisted drum, and shapes like many kinds of flowers,
Or lands apart from sun and moon — how are these measureless ones?
What is a transformation Buddha? And what is a reward-born Buddha?
What is a thusness Buddha? And what is a wisdom Buddha?
Why is it that in the realm of desire one does not attain perfect enlightenment?
And why in the Akanishtha heaven, desire left behind, does one gain bodhi?
When the Sugata enters parinirvana, who will uphold the true Dharma?
How long does the Teacher of Gods abide, and how long does the true Dharma abide?
The siddhanta and the views, how many kinds has each?
The vinaya and the bhiksu's portion — what and by what cause?”
Those noblest sons, the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas all,
By what cause the hundred changes? How the hundred non-receptions fall?
What is the worldly superknowledge? What is the supramundane?
What are the seven stages? Pray you, expound them and make plain.
How many kinds of Sangha are there, and what makes Sangha riven?
What is the treatise of medicine, and whence has it been given?
Wherefore does the great Muni proclaim such words as these:
Kasyapa, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni are myself?’
Wherefore of permanence and ending, and of self and no-self tell,
And wherefore not at every time the real and true meaning reveal,
But for the sake of beings still discriminate the mind’s measure?
For what cause the forest of men and women, haritaki and amalaka,
Mount Kila and the Iron Ring, the Vajra mountains high,
Adorned with boundless jewels, and full of gandharvas nigh?”
The Peerless One, the Knower of the World, heard the verses said,
And of the Mahayana’s gates of perfection, the Buddha-heart is head.
This mind is the solid core, like the firm heart of a tree; it is not the mind of thought and deliberation

Mahamati, listen well; I shall now, in order due,
Speak as you have asked: of arising and of non-arising too,
Of nirvana, emptiness, the instant, and the tending to no self-nature;
Of the Buddhas’ perfections; of the Buddha-sons and Sravakas;
Of Pratyekabuddhas, externalists, and formless practices done;
Of such and such affairs; of Sumeru, the great sea, the mountain;
Of continents and isles and lands, of constellations, sun and moon;
Of externalists, gods, and asuras, liberation, mastery, and superknowledges;
Of the strengths, dhyana, and samadhi, of cessation and the bases of psychic power;
Of the limbs of enlightenment and the factors of the path, of countless meditations;
Of the aggregate-bodies coming and going, of right absorption and cessation’s absorption;
Of rising from samadhi, the teaching of mind, of mind, intellect, and consciousness;
Of the five dharmas of no-self, of self-nature, of perception and the perceived;
And of the two views that appear, of the vehicles and the lineages all;
Of gold and silver, and of mani, the icchantika, the great elements;
Of chaos and the one Buddha, of wisdom, its objects, and the aim attained;
Of beings, of existence and non-existence, elephants, horses, birds, and beasts;
How are they caught? Of similes, of causes, and established truths;
And of the doer and the deed, the tangled wood, delusion, and penetration.
Of the mind’s measure, which appears not; of the stages that reach not one another;
Of the hundred changes, the hundred non-receptions; of medicine and craft;
Of the arts and the various sciences, of the mountains and Sumeru’s land;
Of the great sea and the sun and moon’s measure; of beings low, middle, and high;
How many atoms in each body? In each land, how many lie?
